title: Dementia care systems and caregiver burden
bottleneck: Dementia prevalence will triple by 2050 while no disease-modifying therapy exists, leaving care to fall on unpaid family caregivers with minimal training, respite, or financial support. Health systems are designed around acute episodes, not the decade-long progressive dependency dementia creates.
why_it_blocks: The dementia crisis is a care crisis, not just a drug crisis: without scalable care models, even a future therapy arrives into systems that cannot support patients or their families.
current_state: Anti-amyloid drugs offer marginal slowing at high cost and risk, and several health systems declined coverage. Dementia-friendly community programs and caregiver interventions show modest benefit but are not systematically funded. Dementia villages and caregiver-support programs improve quality of life in pilots, but scaling them requires workforce and funding models that no health system has committed to.
